summary: A 3D chart from data, not geometry: a scatter of points ([x, y, z], sized and coloured by value), bars (categories by series) or a surface z = f(x, y) from a formula. The server picks the axis ranges and ticks, draws a floor and back walls with gridlines, labels the axes from projected points, frames the camera for any aspect and lets the viewer drag to orbit.

type.doc: scatter, bars or surface; auto picks surface for fn, bars for values, else scatter

points.doc: scatter: one entry per point, [x, y, z] or [x, y, z, size] or [x, y, z, size, colour value], or {"x": .., "y": .., "z": .., "size": .., "color": .., "label": "La Paz"}. x runs across, y into the screen, z up. size scales the sphere's area; a label names the point when it is among the highest (annotate)

series.doc: bars: the rows into the screen (y), e.g. ["London", "Seattle"]; each gets a theme colour in a fixed order and a legend entry. Omit for one row

values.doc: bars: one row per series, each with one value per category ([[55, 41, 41], [140, 89, 94]]); one row may be given flat. Bars stand on zero; negative values hang below it

fn.doc: surface: z as a formula in x and y, e.g. "exp(-(x^2 + y^2) / (2 * s^2))" or "x^2 - y^2". ^ is a power, 2x is 2*x; functions sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 sqrt abs exp ln (natural) log (base 10) min max pow hypot floor ceil sign sinh cosh tanh; constants pi, e; names from vars

x.doc: surface: the x domain [from, to] (default [-3, 3]); ticks fall inside it

y.doc: surface: the y domain [from, to] (default: x's)

z.doc: surface: the z range [low, high]; default: the surface's own range over the domain and over every value vars can take, rounded out to ticks (with zero when near). The surface is clamped to it

vars.doc: surface: names the formula uses that the document sets at run time, [{"name": "s", "value": "@sigma", "min": 0.4, "max": 2}] (a slider's variable, a host value); min and max let the server size the z axis for every value. A plain number works too: {"name": "s", "value": 1}

xLabel.doc: Title of the x axis, with its unit: "Area (km²)"

yLabel.doc: Title of the y axis (into the screen). With bars and several series the legend names them instead

zLabel.doc: Title of the vertical axis: "Elevation (m)"; also the colour legend's title when colour shows z

sizeLabel.doc: What a scatter point's size shows (for the description): "Population"

colorLabel.doc: What a scatter point's colour value (its fifth value) shows; the legend's title

colorBy.doc: scatter: z (default; a fifth value wins when the points carry one), size, or none (one colour). bars: series (default with several series) or value (one row is always by value)

annotate.doc: scatter: name this many of the highest labelled points beside them (0 for none)

stems.doc: scatter: a thin line from each point down to the floor, which shows where it stands and how high

spin.doc: Start view: degrees turned about the vertical (0 looks straight along y; 35 is a three-quarter view)

tilt.doc: Start view: degrees looking down (6 to 66); dragging up and down tilts within that range

autorotate.doc: Degrees per second the chart turns by itself (0: only by drag). It repaints every frame while shown; mono never turns

resolution.doc: surface: grid cells per side (8 to 64; default 44, mono 24)

legend.doc: The colour legend below the chart (the ramp with its low and high values, or the series)

height.doc: Chart height in dp, legend not included; ignored with fill

fill.doc: Take the height the parent gives (a weight or a sized box) instead of height

label.doc: Accessibility description; default: what is plotted, the ranges and the highest point

pitfalls: 3D support has not landed in androidx yet (coming): Chart3D plays in the C++ and TypeScript players (rc2image, the web player, the MCP renders) only. Don't use it for a screen that must play on Android today
Give the data, not geometry: points, or categories + values, or a formula. Never compute positions, ticks or camera angles yourself; the server maps the data into the box and picks round ranges
Colour by value is five steps of one blue (light = low, dark = high), not a continuous gradient: each mesh takes one paint colour. Values in one step look the same; the legend shows the steps' range

A surface's colour bands follow its grid cells, so their edges are stepped at the grid's size; raise resolution for smoother bands (each step costs render time: five copies of the mesh are evaluated every frame)
A variable in a surface formula (vars) must be read after whatever writes it: put a Slider above the chart in the document, since a slider's live value is its own variable only from the slider on
Every mesh draw composites a window-sized buffer in the players, so render time grows with the number of draws: a scatter of 50 points is about 60 draws. Keep scatters under about 100 points

Labels are 2D text placed from projected points: tick values on the floor edges nearest the viewer and up a back corner, titles beyond them. At very small sizes (under about 180 dp) they crowd: give the chart room or drop the titles
Mono draws points and bars in the text colour with shading (bars as boxes with drawn edges) and the surface as a hidden-line wireframe; size and position carry the data, colour does not
